multiplechoiceresponse.p: Three tickets: (a) the CEO's laptop will not power on, (b) a mouse is unresponsive, (c) the whole sales floor cannot reach the CRM. Which do you work first?

choice.div: (c) — an outage affecting a whole team and a core service.
(a) — the CEO is the most senior person.
(b) — it is the quickest to close.

div.p: Priority is impact times urgency. A team-wide outage of a core service outranks a single device, however senior its user. (b) can be slotted in while (c) is being worked if it is genuinely trivial.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Eight users in one office report the same Wi-Fi failure within minutes. You should:

choice.div: Treat it as one incident, check the access point, and communicate.
Work eight separate tickets in order.
Tell each user to reboot and close the tickets.

div.p: Related tickets are one incident with one root cause. Working them separately wastes time and hides the scope.

choiceresponse.p: Which must be included in an escalation? Select all that apply.

choice.div: What you already tried, and the result

div.p: An escalation is a request for a decision. Give the next tier everything they need to act without starting over.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A fix worked yesterday and the same user is back with the same problem. The best next step is:

choice.div: Find the root cause and document it, rather than applying the same band-aid.
Apply the same fix, close it, and move on.

div.p: A recurring problem means the cause was never fixed. Investigate the root cause and write it up so the next recurrence is prevented, not repeated.
